final_assessment: Q-crc-20 opened and deliberately deferred: can in-context token usage be tracked generally, outside reviews. Sal raised both the question and its overlap concern (IDEs already track usage). The finding worth keeping is that the blocker is a UNIT MISMATCH rather than missing data — orbit's unit is the command, a token budget's unit is the session, and they do not line up in either direction, so recording per-session usage would require orbit to learn what a session IS. The distinguishing line is ATTRIBUTION: raw usage is commodity that an IDE does better, while usage attributed to a workstream (this change, this stage, this program) is something no IDE can produce because none knows what a change is. Deferred with a specific trigger rather than vaguely: revisit only after Q-crc-18's reading surface exists, because building capture first would create a fourth instance of the write-only pattern already recorded in the status log, and the entire argument for recording effort is that something eventually consumes it.

boot_sequence.why: R-crc-11(a)-(i) and the cost shape; Q-crc-19 blocks rc02c and rc04; Q-crc-20 deferred behind Q-crc-18's reading surface
